To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in the Netherlands it is mainly feelings such as being needed or feeling obliged that increase the chances of informal care being provided, whereas in Southern Europe the family’s responsibility for providing care is less important.
in the Netherlands and Southern Europe the main motives for providing care are different, and that the main motives in the Netherlands are more likely to lead to informal care being provided.
the Dutch give more informal care than Southern Europeans because of their motives, but that if they had the same motives, they would give less care.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role played by motivation in the provision of informal care, and the consequences of different motivations for informal care provision.
the question of how the provision of informal care by middle aged and elderly persons can be influenced by the motives underlying the decision to give care.
the question of whether a greater emphasis on family responsibility will lead to an increase in the amount of informal care given, and if not, why this is the case.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the motives for informal care are complex and that the effect of the motives differs between countries.
in the Netherlands the motives of the carer are important in explaining the giving of care.
the Dutch are more motivated by feelings of obligation, and less motivated by feelings of being needed, to give informal care than are their European counterparts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the more family responsibility and obligation are stressed in policy, the less informal care is given.
the Dutch are not more likely to give informal care, but that they do give more informal care.
the Dutch are more motivated by the need to care than their Southern European counterparts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
policy measures that aim to increase informal caregiving should be carefully considered, because they may not achieve the intended result.
it is important to look at the motives that lead people to give informal care.
the motives of informal carers should not be ignored when considering the future of informal care.
